newsitem.title: UK: Mark/yen seen riding for a fall after G7.
newsitem.headline: Mark/yen seen riding for a fall after G7.

text.p: The mark/yen cross is one to watch in the aftermath of Saturday's Group-of-Seven G7 meeting, with the market looking for greater upside for dollar/mark than dollar/yen.
Dealers and analysts are of the opinion that the upside potential for dollar/yen is more limited for several reasons.
1) Comments from the Japanese G7 delegation about the yen's weakness were more hard-line compared with Germany's about the level of dollar/mark.
2) Dollar/yen has risen 55 percent since the lows in Q2 1995 compared with a 23 percent dollar rise on the mark.
3) The Bank of Japan has a lot of ammunition, over $200 billion in reserves, it can call on to keep dollar/yen down.
4) There is a degree of self interest among the G7 who, analysts reckon, are worried that a steep yen fall could hit fragile Japanese markets hard and have a knock-on effect globally.
5) Germany is probably much less worried than Japan about the level of its currency versus the dollar and the authorities there would not lose too much sleep should the mark ease further.
Analysts said all this adds up to a falling mark/yen as the dollar puts more pressure on the mark than the yen.
"If dollar/mark trades at 1.6750 (its recent peak) and dollar/yen is at 125 you could find the BoJ on the other side of dollar/yen," said one trader.
Technically mark/yen looks like it has already turned with three successive lower peaks on the chart at around 75.90 on October 30, 75.30 on December 31 and 75.10 on February 5.
On top of this, a downtrend line drawn in from the 91.13 peak in August 1990 coincides with this series of descending tops.
Mark/yen was trading around 74.10/12 at 1400 GMT compared with Friday's 74.40/43.
